tags.name: Scouts
tags.description:
Scouts are the proactive tests that you configure to monitor the availability and health of various resources. There are different types of Scouts, depending on the type of resource you want to test. Within each type, there are sub-types which determine which test is performed and the available test configuration options.

Scouts are initiated from Hives, which are either hosted in the cloud (Cloud Hives), or installed on-premises (Custom Hives).

tags.name: Tests
tags.description: The output of the scout tests

tags.name: Hives
tags.description:
Hives are the locations from which Scouts (tests) are initiated.

Custom Hives allow you to test internal resources from within your network. They must be installed on a computer with access to your network.

Cloud hives allow you to test publicly available resources from locations throughout the world. They are hosted and managed by Scoutbees, and require no configuration.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: Scouts can be configured to trigger an alert when certain conditions are met. You can use endpoints to get a list of alerts from all Scouts, a list of Scouts that have triggered an alert, and a list of alerts from a specific Scout.

AlertTriggerSettings.title: Alert Trigger Settings
AlertTriggerSettings.description: Settings that control when and how alerts are triggered.

sendOnStatusChange.description:
If `true`, notifications are sent only when the alert status changes, to prevent excessive notifications. This means that if the Scout
triggers the alert 10 times in a row, you'll receive one notification when the Scout first triggers the alert, and another notification
when the Scout recovers.

If `false`, notifications are sent every time the alert triggers. This means that if something goes wrong and the Scout
starts triggering the alert, you'll receive a notification every time the Scout runs.

consecutiveMatchCount.description:
Number of consecutive test results that must match the alert conditions before 
the alert is triggered. This helps prevent false positives from temporary issues.

attachOutput.description:
Relevant for Shell Scouts only. Attach the test output to alert notifications. When enabled, the notification 
payload will include additional details about the test result that triggered the alert.

evaluationScope.description:
Scope for evaluating consecutive matches.

- `GLOBAL`: Evaluate consecutive matches across all specified hives (or all hives if targetHives is not specified).
  The alert triggers when the required consecutive count is met across any combination of the target hives.
- `PER_HIVE`: Evaluate consecutive matches separately for each hive. 
  The alert triggers when any single hive meets the required consecutive count.

targetHives.title: Target Hives
targetHives.description:
Sets which hives to include in the consecutive match evaluation.
This is only used when `evaluationScope` is set to `GLOBAL`. 
If not specified when evaluationScope is GLOBAL, all hives are evaluated.

AlertConditionObjectCitrix.title: Citrix
AlertConditionObjectCitrix.description:
To create an Alert policy based on a single condition (for example, status == 'failure'), select `Condition`.

To create an Alert policy based on multiple conditions (for example, status == 'failure' OR jitter > 30ms), select `Condition group`, choose the operator for the conditions in the group (AND/OR), and add your conditions.
You can nest condition groups (to combine AND and OR statements) by adding a condition group within another condition group.

AlertTerminalRuleCitrix.title: Condition
AlertTerminalRuleCitrix.description: A single alert condition that evaluates a test result property.

field.description:
The test result property to compare against.

| Property Name | Description | Type |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| status | Overall status for the test, either **`success`** or **`failure`**. | string |
| failReason | The reason that the test failed. | string |
| imgAnomalyScore | Image Anomaly Score. | number (float) |
| authPhase | Authentication Duration (seconds). | number (float) |
| connPhase | Connecting to Session Duration (seconds). | number (float) |
| durationReady | Total Time to Session Ready (secconds). | number (float) |
| enumTime | Resources Enumeration Duration (seconds). | number (integer) |
| ready | Session Handoff (Ready) Duration (seconds). | number (float) |
| sess | Session Initialization Duration (seconds). | number (integer) |
| loginAttempts | Login Attempts. | number (integer) |
| icaTime | ICA Download Duration (seconds). | number (integer) |
| serverName | Server Name. | string |

operator.description:
Comparison operator for evaluating the condition.
* For string fields, use `==`, `!=`, `contains`, `not_contains`.
* For number fields, use `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `==`, `!=`
* For boolean fields, use `==`, `!=`.

value.description: Value to compare against. The data type must match the data type of the test result property in the `field` parameter.

WebTransactionFlow.title: Web Transaction Step
WebTransactionFlow.description:
A single step in the Web Transactions flow.

Each step has an `actionType` that dictates which of `locator` and `extras` you must supply, and what shape they take:

| `actionType`        | `locator`               | `extras`                                        |
|---------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `click`             | required                | omit (or `null`)                                |
| `mouse_hover`       | required                | omit (or `null`)                                |
| `step_in_iframe`    | required                | omit (or `null`)                                |
| `mfa`               | required                | omit (or `null`)                                |
| `move_mouse`        | omit (or `null`)        | omit (or `null`)                                |
| `step_out_iframe`   | omit (or `null`)        | omit (or `null`)                                |
| `insert_text`       | required                | `{ text, isPassword? }`                         |
| `press_key`         | omit (or `null`)        | `{ key }`                                       |
| `assert`            | required                | `{ text, operator? }`                           |
| `wait`              | required                | `{ expectedCondition, timeout? }`               |
| `switch_tab`        | omit (or `null`)        | `{ tab }`                                       |

stepNumber.description: Position of the step in the flow (1-based).

locator.description: How to locate the target DOM element. Required only for the `actionType` values marked "required" above.

value.description: The selector expression itself (XPath / CSS selector / JS path).

extras.description: Action-specific parameters. The exact shape depends on `actionType`; pass `null` or omit for actions that don't take any.

text.description: The text to type into the located element.

isPassword.description: Mark the value as a password. Stored encrypted; not returned in GET responses.

text.description: The substring expected to appear in the located element.

operator.description: Comparison operator. `contains` is the only supported value today.

expectedCondition.description: The DOM condition the Scout waits for before proceeding to the next step.

tags.description:
A list of tag value UUIDs to associate with the Scout.

Tag values can be retrieved from [GET /v1/organizations/{orgId}/tags](orgtagspubliccontroller_getall). 
Each tag object contains a list of values, each with its own `id`. To assign a tag, provide the `id` of the desired tag value.

**Example:** Given the following tag object:
```json
{
  "id": "047b0a09-a33e-45fd-b579-a098ec60d0b5",
  "key": "Database",
  "values": [
    { "id": "07725341-3335-4f4a-a6d7-f64302546c7e", "label": "SQL", "color": "stone" },
    { "id": "2e7aa044-6786-406d-bd00-f43921831099", "label": "NoSQL", "color": "stone" }
  ]
}
```
To assign the Database:SQL tag, include `"07725341-3335-4f4a-a6d7-f64302546c7e"` in the list.

When you update tags, all existing tags are replaced with the ones you provide.
